solution.explanation: 'You look tired' is a statement: 'told him that he looked tired' (tense backshifted). 'Why don't you rest?' is a suggestion, not a real question, so it is reported with 'suggested that he should rest'.
steps: Statement → told him that he looked tired
'Why don't you ...?' = suggestion → suggested that he should ...
solution.why_others_wrong: Keeping 'looks' and 'why don't you' copies the direct words. 'Suggested him to rest' is wrong: 'suggest' takes a that-clause or -ing, not object + infinitive. 'Said him' is wrong ('say' needs 'to').
solution.final_answer: Option B: She told him that he looked tired and suggested that he should rest for a while.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the verb form that correctly fills the blank.
The goods ______ loaded onto the lorry late last night.

solution.concept: 'Goods' (merchandise) is always plural and takes a plural verb
solution.explanation: 'Goods' has no singular form in this sense and is treated as plural; the time is past ('last night'): 'The goods were loaded ...'.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Was' and 'is' are singular, and 'is' is also present. 'Has loaded' would make the goods do the loading.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the verb form that correctly fills the blank.
The United States ______ a federal system of government.

solution.concept: A country's name that is plural in form takes a singular verb
solution.explanation: 'The United States' names one country, so it takes a singular verb: 'The United States has a federal system of government.'
steps: Subject: one country, plural in form
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Have', 'are having' and 'were having' treat the country as plural; the last two also use 'have' (possess) in a continuous form.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the verb form that correctly fills the blank.
All the riches of the old merchant ______ not able to buy him a single night of peaceful sleep.

solution.concept: 'Riches' (wealth) is a plural noun and takes a plural verb
solution.explanation: 'Riches' has no singular in this sense and is always plural, so the verb is plural; the story is in the past: 'All the riches ... were not able to buy him ...'.
steps: 'of the old merchant' does not change the number
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Was' and 'is' treat 'riches' as singular. 'Has not able' is not a correct verb form.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the option that correctly fills the blank(s).
So far this season, our school team ______ four matches and lost none.

solution.concept: Present perfect with 'so far': a period that runs up to now
solution.explanation: 'So far this season' covers the time from the start of the season up to now, which calls for the present perfect: 'has won four matches and (has) lost none'.
steps: Time marker: so far (up to now)
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Had won' needs a later past moment to refer to. 'Wins' and 'is winning' cannot count matches already played up to now.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the option that correctly fills the blank(s).
The window is still open and the jewellery box is empty; the thief seems ______ through the window.

solution.concept: Perfect infinitive (to have + past participle) for an action earlier than the main verb
solution.explanation: The seeming is present ('seems'), but the escape happened earlier. An earlier action after 'seem' takes the perfect infinitive: 'the thief seems to have escaped through the window.'
steps: Earlier action → perfect infinitive: 'to have escaped'
solution.why_others_wrong: 'To escape' would describe a present or habitual action. 'Seems escaping' is not standard, and 'to be escaped' is a wrong passive.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the option that correctly fills the blank(s).
Yesterday morning, she assured her manager that by six o'clock that evening she ______ the report.

solution.concept: Sequence of tenses: future perfect seen from the past = would have + past participle
solution.explanation: Her promise was made in the past ('assured', 'yesterday morning') about a time that is also past now (six o'clock that evening). 'Will have finished' moves back to 'would have finished'.
steps: Future perfect from a past viewpoint
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Will have finished' ignores the past reporting verb, and six o'clock yesterday is no longer in the future. 'Has finished' and 'had been finishing' do not express a promise about a deadline.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the option that correctly fills the blank(s).
Meena is ______ only daughter of her parents.

solution.concept: 'The' before 'only' when it picks out a single, particular person or thing
solution.explanation: 'Only daughter' names the one and only daughter, so the definite article is needed: 'Meena is the only daughter of her parents.'
solution.why_others_wrong: 'A' and 'an' would suggest one of several, which contradicts 'only'. Without an article the noun phrase is incomplete.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the option that correctly fills the blank(s).
______ Andaman and Nicobar Islands lie in ______ Bay of Bengal.

solution.concept: 'The' with groups of islands and with bays named 'the Bay of ...'
solution.explanation: A group of islands takes 'the' (the Andaman and Nicobar Islands), and so does a bay named with 'of' (the Bay of Bengal).
solution.why_others_wrong: Dropping either 'the' breaks one of the two rules. 'An' is singular and cannot go with 'Islands'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the option that correctly fills the blank.
The old soldier is blind ______ one eye but still reads the newspaper every morning.

solution.explanation: Loss of sight in one eye is expressed as 'blind in one eye'.

questions.subject: English Language

Choose the connector that best fills the blank.
The scholarship is open only to first-time students; ______, anyone who has already earned a degree cannot apply.

solution.concept: 'In other words' introduces a restatement of the same point
solution.explanation: 'Open only to first-time students' and 'anyone who already has a degree cannot apply' say the same thing in two ways. A restatement is introduced by 'in other words'.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'On the other hand' and 'by contrast' signal a contrast, and 'even so' signals a surprising contrast; the second clause does not contrast with the first.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question_text:
Choose the connector that best fills the blank.
The new rules will add to the paperwork of small lenders. ______, they will give depositors far better protection.

solution.concept: 'Be that as it may' = even though that is true (accepting a point, then moving to a stronger one)
solution.explanation: The opening sentence admits a drawback (more paperwork); the next gives an outweighing benefit. 'Be that as it may' accepts the first point and turns to the second.
steps: Sentence 2: a benefit that outweighs it
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Inasmuch as' (= because), 'Lest' (= for fear that) and 'So long as' (= provided that) introduce clauses, and none of them can open a full sentence that answers a drawback.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Be that as it may

No penalty is levied on premature conversion of FCNR(B) balances into RFC accounts by NRIs on return, so III is wrong (penalties do apply to conversion between FCNR(B) and NRE).
steps: III: false – conversion into RFC on return is penalty-free
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Two NRIs return to India for good and immediately ask their banks to convert NRE term deposits into Resident Foreign Currency (RFC) accounts: X's deposit has run for 8 months, Y's for 18 months. Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, what interest do they get on the NRE deposits?

options.text: X: the contracted rate less a penalty; Y: the contracted rate
X: at most the rate on RFC savings deposits; Y: the contracted rate — and no premature withdrawal penalty for either
X: nothing; Y: the RFC savings rate
Both: the contracted rate, plus a penalty for premature withdrawal

solution.explanation: If the NRE deposit has not run for the minimum period of one year, interest on conversion into RFC is paid at a rate not exceeding the RFC savings rate (X); otherwise at the contracted rate (Y). No premature withdrawal penalty is levied on NRE deposits converted into RFC accounts.
solution.why_others_wrong: No penalty applies to NRE → RFC conversion; X is not denied interest; Y gets the contracted rate.
solution.final_answer: Option B: X: at most the rate on RFC savings deposits; Y: the contracted rate — and no premature withdrawal penalty for either

If the NRE deposit has not run for a minimum period of one year, interest shall be paid at a rate not exceeding the rate payable on savings deposits held in RFC accounts. In all other cases, interest shall be paid at the contracted rate
No penalty shall be levied for premature withdrawal of NRE term deposits for conversion into RFC account

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the DEA Fund procedures in RBI's Commercial Banks – Miscellaneous Directions, 2025:
I. A bank may designate up to 10 officers as authorised signatories to operate its DEA Fund account jointly.
II. A bank submits only one consolidated claim per month to the Fund, during the first 10 working days.
III. Interest payable from the Fund on a claim accrues from the date the depositor opened the account.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Banks may designate a maximum of 10 officers as joint authorised signatories (I) and submit one consolidated claim a month during the first 10 working days (II). Interest from the Fund accrues only from the date the balance was transferred to the Fund to the date of payment, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – from date of transfer to the Fund
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

A bank shall ... submit claim from the Fund in e-Kuber system during the first 10 working days of every month. A bank shall submit only one consolidated claim per month
The interest payable, if any, from the Fund on a claim shall accrue only from the date on which the balance in an account was transferred to the Fund to the date of payment

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:

III. Paytm Payments Bank Limited was included in the Second Schedule (Gazette of 7 September 2026).

Rabobank, a foreign bank, ceased to be a banking company under Section 36A(2) and was excluded from the Second Schedule, both notified on 24 June 2026 and published on 2 July 2026 (II). Paytm Payments Bank was excluded from, not included in, the Second Schedule by the notification published on 7 September 2026, so III is wrong.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025, what floor applies to interest rates on fixed rate loans of tenor below three years?

options.text: There is no floor; banks may price them freely
They cannot be lower than the Bank Rate
They cannot be lower than the benchmark rate for a similar tenor
They must equal the policy repo rate plus 2 per cent

solution.explanation: Banks may offer fixed or floating rates, but interest on fixed rate loans of tenor below three years must not be less than the benchmark rate for similar tenor; and there can be no lending below the benchmark for loans linked to it.
steps: Fixed rate, tenor < 3 years → ≥ benchmark for similar tenor
solution.why_others_wrong: No repo-plus-2% rule exists; there is a floor; the Bank Rate is not the reference.
solution.final_answer: Option C: They cannot be lower than the benchmark rate for a similar tenor

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the MCLR system in RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025, the spread over MCLR consists of business strategy and credit risk premium. What restriction applies to these components?

options.text: They must be identical for all borrowers
They must each be at least 1 percentage point
They can be negative to win large borrowers
They can be positive or zero, but cannot be negative

solution.explanation: The spread components — business strategy and credit risk premium — must have either a positive value or be zero; they cannot be negative, so loans cannot be priced below MCLR through a negative spread.
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no 1-point minimum; negative spreads are barred; spreads vary across borrowers by risk.
solution.final_answer: Option D: They can be positive or zero, but cannot be negative

fact_checks.claim: The components of the spread i.e. business strategy and Credit risk premium shall have either a positive value or be zero. In other words, the spread components cannot be negative

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the liquidity management framework of 30 September 2025, how much advance notice does RBI ordinarily give market participants before conducting a repo/reverse repo liquidity operation?

options.text: At least one day, though it may announce an operation on the same day when circumstances warrant
No notice; all operations are announced at the start of the auction window
At least one fortnight, matching the reserve maintenance period

solution.explanation: To reduce uncertainty about the tenor, quantum and timing of operations, RBI gives participants at least one day's advance notice, while retaining the option of same-day operations when warranted.
steps: Ordinarily ≥ 1 day notice; same-day possible when warranted
solution.why_others_wrong: One week or a fortnight is not the rule; operations are not announced only at the window.
solution.final_answer: Option B: At least one day, though it may announce an operation on the same day when circumstances warrant

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: At its 57th meeting (29 September–1 October 2025), the MPC kept the repo rate at 5.50% even though inflation had turned 'even more benign'. What reason did it give?

options.text: The Government had asked RBI not to cut rates
It was prudent to let the front-loaded monetary policy actions and recent fiscal measures play out and wait for clarity on trade uncertainties
Liquidity was in deficit, so a cut would not be transmitted
Inflation was above the upper tolerance limit

solution.explanation: The MPC noted that the impact of front-loaded rate cuts and recent fiscal measures (including GST rationalisation) was still playing out and trade uncertainties were unfolding, so it considered it prudent to wait before charting the next course; it continued with the neutral stance.
steps: Space existed, but waited for past actions to play out
solution.why_others_wrong: Inflation was low (2.1% in August 2025); the Government does not direct the MPC's vote; liquidity was not cited.
solution.final_answer: Option B: It was prudent to let the front-loaded monetary policy actions and recent fiscal measures play out and wait for clarity on trade uncertainties

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

solution.explanation: The revised framework allows Standalone Primary Dealers (SPDs) access to the SDF, overnight reverse repo operations and all repo operations, irrespective of tenor. (They had been allowed into all repo operations from March 2025.)

solution.why_others_wrong: NBFCs, mutual funds and payment operators are not LAF participants.

III. At its meeting ending 1 October 2025 the MPC changed the stance to accommodative.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: April 2025: along with a 25 bps cut, the MPC changed the stance from neutral to accommodative (I). August 2025: unanimous pause at 5.50% with all members for neutral (II). October 2025: the MPC continued with the neutral stance, so III is wrong.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Compare the members who attended the MPC meeting of February 2025 (Malhotra, Nagesh Kumar, Saugata Bhattacharya, Ram Singh, Rajiv Ranjan, M. Rajeshwar Rao) with those of February 2026. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Two of the three Government-appointed members had changed
Dr. Poonam Gupta had replaced Prof. Ram Singh as a Government-appointed member
The three Government-appointed members were the same, while Dr. Poonam Gupta and Shri Indranil Bhattacharyya had replaced Dr. Rajiv Ranjan and Shri M. Rajeshwar Rao
All six members were the same

solution.explanation: Both meetings had Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Shri Saugata Bhattacharya and Prof. Ram Singh as the external members (appointed for four years from October 2024). The RBI side changed: in February 2026 the members were Governor Malhotra, Deputy Governor Dr. Poonam Gupta and Executive Director Shri Indranil Bhattacharyya (nominated by the Central Board), in place of Shri Rajeshwar Rao and Dr. Rajiv Ranjan.
steps: RBI members: Gupta and Bhattacharyya in place of Rao and Ranjan

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about loans exempted from the benchmark-linked pricing rules (Base Rate, MCLR, external benchmark) in RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025:
I. Advances to a bank's depositors against their own deposits are exempt.
II. Advances to the bank's own employees, including retired employees, are exempt.
III. Loans under Government schemes that prescribe the interest rate must still be priced at or above the bank's MCLR.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Directions exempt, among others, loans under Government schemes where the bank must charge the scheme's rate, WCTL/FITL under restructuring, refinance-scheme loans (to the extent refinanced), advances to depositors against their own deposits (I), advances to employees including retired employees (II), and advances to the CEO/whole-time directors. Scheme loans are exempt, so III is wrong.
steps: III: scheme-rate loans are exempt – false
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's USD/INR buy/sell swap auction of December 2025 (USD 5 billion, 36 months):
I. Bids were quoted as the premium, in paisa, that banks were willing to pay RBI for the tenor of the swap.
II. It was a multiple-price auction: successful bids were accepted at their own quoted premium.
III. Bids were arranged in ascending order of premium, and those below the cut-off were accepted.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Participants bid the premium (paisa, two decimals) they would pay RBI (I); the auction was multiple-price, with successful bids accepted at their quoted premium (II). Bids were arranged in descending order, and those at or above the cut-off premium succeeded while lower bids were rejected, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – descending order; bids at/above cut-off succeed

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's liquidity framework as it stands in November 2026:
I. The symmetric corridor finalised in September 2025 is retained, with the SDF and MSF 25 bps on either side of the repo rate.
II. The weighted average call rate remains the operating target, while RBI also tracks rates in other overnight money market segments.
III. The 14-day variable rate repo/reverse repo remains the main operation for managing transient liquidity.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The September 2025 framework retained the symmetric corridor (I) and the WACR as operating target, with RBI also tracking other overnight segments (II). The 14-day VRR/VRRR was discontinued as the main operation; transient liquidity is managed mainly through 7-day operations, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – 7-day operations are now the main tool
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The existing symmetric corridor system is retained, with policy repo rate at the middle of the corridor and standing deposit facility (SDF) and marginal standing facility (MSF), which are 25 bps on either side of the policy repo rate ... The Reserve Bank will, however, continue to keep track of rates in other overnight money market segments

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

The Government had cut the fiscal deficit target
Inflation had risen above the 6% upper tolerance limit
The US Federal Reserve had cut rates by 50 bps

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

solution.explanation: The Bank Rate went 5% (26 September 1964) → 6% (17 February 1965); it was cut to 5% on 2 March 1968 and restored to 6% on 9 January 1971.
solution.why_others_wrong: 26 Sep 1964 was 5%; 9 Jan 1971 was a return to 6%; 2 Mar 1968 was a cut to 5%.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the liquidity management framework of September 2025, how much can an individual bank draw under the Marginal Standing Facility, whose rate is the same as the Bank Rate?

options.text: Against its excess SLR holdings plus up to 2% of its NDTL (as at the end of the second preceding fortnight) below the stipulated SLR
Up to 2% of NDTL only, with no use of excess SLR

solution.explanation: The annex to the framework says banks can draw MSF funds against their excess SLR holdings plus up to 2% of NDTL outstanding at the end of the second preceding fortnight, below the stipulated SLR.
steps: MSF = excess SLR + dip of up to 2% of NDTL
solution.why_others_wrong: Excess SLR also counts; MSF is collateralised; 1% was the 2011 limit.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Against its excess SLR holdings plus up to 2% of its NDTL (as at the end of the second preceding fortnight) below the stipulated SLR

fact_checks.claim: Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) | Individual banks can draw funds against their excess SLR holdings + up to 2 per cent of their respective NDTL outstanding as at the end of the second preceding fortnight, below the stipulated SLR

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
The Bank Rate was 6.50% after the MPC decision of February 2025. After the June 2025 decision it was 5.75%. Consider:
I. The Bank Rate fell by 75 bps between these two decisions.
II. The Bank Rate moved automatically with the MSF rate as the repo rate was cut.
III. The Bank Rate remained 50 bps above the repo rate throughout.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: 6.50 − 5.75 = 0.75 → 75 bps (I). The Bank Rate is aligned with the MSF rate and changes automatically with it (II). The MSF/Bank Rate is 25 bps above the repo rate (6.50 vs 6.25; 5.75 vs 5.50), so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out II.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate to 6.50 per cent
the marginal standing facility (MSF) rate and the Bank Rate to 5.75 per cent
This rate has been aligned with the MSF rate and, changes automatically as and when the MSF rate changes alongside policy repo rate changes

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Governor's statement of 7 October 2026 cited sugar as one item behind broad-based food price pressures. What did it say about sugar prices?

options.text: They were unchanged due to export restrictions
They rose about 34% from early July to ₹64/kg by end-August, before retreating in September
They fell 34% because of a bumper crop

solution.explanation: Sugar prices rose about 34% from early July to ₹64/kg by end-August on a tight demand-supply balance and precautionary stocking; Government measures (export restrictions, stock limits, duty-free imports of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar) eased them, and prices retreated in September.
solution.why_others_wrong: Prices rose, not fell; they did not double; they were not unchanged.
solution.final_answer: Option B: They rose about 34% from early July to ₹64/kg by end-August, before retreating in September

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The WPI (base 2022-23) for all commodities was 110.8 in August 2026 and 112.5 in September 2026, when year-on-year WPI inflation was 11.39% (9.92% in August). Which statement is correct?

options.text: The index fell month-on-month while year-on-year inflation rose
The index rose about 1.5% month-on-month, and year-on-year inflation rose by about 1.5 percentage points
The index rose about 1.7% month-on-month, and year-on-year inflation rose by 1.7 percentage points

solution.explanation: Month-on-month: 112.5 ÷ 110.8 − 1 ≈ 1.53%. Year-on-year inflation rose from 9.92% to 11.39%, i.e. 1.47 percentage points. The 11.39% compares September 2026 with September 2025, not with August.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11.39% is the y-o-y rate; the index rose; 1.7 points is the index-point change, not a percentage.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The index rose about 1.5% month-on-month, and year-on-year inflation rose by about 1.5 percentage points

fact_checks.claim: All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for September 2026 is 11.39 per cent on year-on-year (YoY) basis, compared to 9.92 per cent in August 2026. The index for All Commodities for September 2026 stands at 112.5, whereas it was 110.8 in August 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Where do commercial banks show the provisions held against standard assets in their balance sheet, according to RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025?

options.text: Netted from gross advances, like provisions on NPAs
Deducted from gross NPAs to arrive at net NPAs
Separately, as 'Contingent Provisions against Standard Assets' under 'Other Liabilities and Provisions – Others'
As part of the Interest Suspense Account

solution.explanation: Standard asset provisions are not netted from gross advances and are not reckoned for arriving at net NPAs; they are shown separately as 'Contingent Provisions against Standard Assets' under 'Other Liabilities and Provisions – Others' in Schedule 5 of the balance sheet.
steps: Shown in Schedule 5 as contingent provisions
solution.why_others_wrong: The Directions expressly bar netting them from gross advances or using them for net NPAs; interest suspense is a different account.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Separately, as 'Contingent Provisions against Standard Assets' under 'Other Liabilities and Provisions – Others'

fact_checks.claim: The provisions towards standard assets need not be netted from gross advances but shown separately as 'Contingent Provisions against Standard Assets' under 'Other Liabilities and Provisions Others' in Schedule 5 of the balance sheet
The provisions on standard assets shall not be reckoned for arriving at net NPAs

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, overdue receivables representing the positive mark-to-market value of a derivative contract are classified as NPA if they remain unpaid for how long from the specified due date?

solution.explanation: In respect of derivative transactions, overdue receivables representing positive mark-to-market value become NPA if they remain unpaid for 90 days from the specified due date for payment.
steps: Unpaid 90 days from due date → NPA
solution.why_others_wrong: 30 and 60 days mark SMA stages; 180 days is the limit for reviewing credit limits.

fact_checks.claim: in respect of derivative transactions, the overdue receivables representing positive mark-to-market value of a derivative contract, remain unpaid for a period of 90 days from the specified due date for payment

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank acquires a borrower's immovable property in satisfaction of its claims (a 'specified non-financial asset', SNFA). Under RBI's Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025, the bank's policy must set a maximum period for its disposal not exceeding:

solution.explanation: An SNFA is an immovable asset acquired by a bank in full or part satisfaction of its claims, including non-banking assets. The bank's policy must cover the limit on SNFAs as a share of total assets, eligibility, delegation, recovery efforts before acquisition and a maximum disposal period not exceeding seven years.
steps: SNFA = immovable asset taken over in satisfaction of claims
solution.why_others_wrong: One, three and ten years are not the ceiling in the Directions.

fact_checks.claim: 'specified non-financial asset' (SNFA) means an immovable asset acquired by a bank in satisfaction or part satisfaction of its claims on the borrower

Such provisions shall specify inter-alia the limit on SNFAs as a share of total assets, eligibility criteria, delegation matrix, recovery efforts to be explored before acquisition and maximum period for disposal not exceeding seven years

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under Section 31 of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, a secured creditor cannot use the Act's enforcement provisions where the amount due is less than what share of the principal amount and interest?

solution.concept: Exclusions under Section 31 of the SARFAESI Act
solution.explanation: Section 31(j) excludes cases where the amount due is less than 20% of the principal amount and interest thereon; such dues must be recovered through other routes such as the DRT. Section 31(i) separately excludes security interest created in agricultural land.
steps: Section 31 lists cases where SARFAESI does not apply
Clause (j): amount due < 20% of principal and interest
solution.why_others_wrong: 10%, 25% and 50% are not the threshold in Section 31(j).

fact_checks.claim: Section 31(j): the Act does not apply where the amount due is less than twenty per cent of the principal amount and interest thereon
SARFAESI proceedings can be initiated only if the outstanding due payable by the borrower is more than 20% of principal and interest

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025, a bank must normally classify assets through an automated system. If, exceptionally, a manual intervention overrides the system classification, what is required?

options.text: A single authorisation by the branch manager, with no logs required
Prior approval of RBI for each override
Approval of the statutory auditor, with logs kept for one year
At least two-level authorisation, with logs of the override stored for at least three years

solution.explanation: Manual intervention is to be avoided; where it is unavoidable it needs at least two-level authorisation under the Board-approved delegation, and logs (date and time stamp, reason, user IDs, names, designations and account details) must be stored for at least three years without tampering.
solution.why_others_wrong: Auditor approval, RBI approval per case and single authorisation without logs are not the rule.
solution.final_answer: Option D: At least two-level authorisation, with logs of the override stored for at least three years

fact_checks.claim: In any exceptional circumstance where manual intervention is required to override the System classification, it shall have at least two level authorisation
These logs shall also be stored for a minimum period of three years and not be tampered with

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An official of an asset reconstruction company (ARC) was part of the committee that approved the acquisition of a financial asset. According to RBI's FAQs on ARCs (September 2026), what role can that official play when a settlement proposal for the same asset comes up?

options.text: The official may approve it with the Board's prior consent
The official may process it but not approve it
None; the official cannot be part of processing or approving the settlement in any capacity
The official may approve it if the settlement is above the acquisition price

solution.explanation: To segregate acquisition and settlement, any official who was part of the acquisition of a financial asset (individually or in a committee) shall not be part of either processing or approving the settlement proposal for that asset, in any capacity.
steps: Acquisition and settlement must be segregated
Acquiring official → no role in settlement
solution.why_others_wrong: No exception exists for price, a processing-only role or Board consent.
solution.final_answer: Option C: None; the official cannot be part of processing or approving the settlement in any capacity

fact_checks.claim: any official who was part of the acquisition (as an individual or part of a committee) of the concerned financial asset shall not be part of either processing or approving the proposal for settlement of the same financial asset, in any capacity

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements under RBI's IRACP Directions, 2025:
I. Specific provisions that a bank voluntarily makes on NPAs at rates higher than the regulatory minimum are treated as floating provisions.
II. Such additional provisions on NPAs may be netted off from gross NPAs to arrive at net NPAs.
III. Floating provisions cannot be reversed by credit to the profit and loss account.
IV. Amounts held in the Interest Suspense Account are reckoned as part of provisions.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.concept: Additional provisions, floating provisions and interest suspense
solution.explanation: Voluntary higher provisions on NPAs (Board-approved and consistently applied) are not floating provisions, and like the regulatory minimum they may be netted from gross NPAs. Floating provisions can only be used for specific provisions in extraordinary circumstances and are never reversed to P&L. Interest suspense balances are not provisions; they are deducted from the advance before provisioning.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing I or IV are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option D: II and III only

fact_checks.claim: Such additional provisions shall not be considered as floating provisions. The additional provisions for NPAs, like the minimum regulatory provision on NPAs, may be netted off from gross NPAs to arrive at the net NPAs
Floating provisions shall not be reversed by credit to the profit and loss account
Amounts held in Interest Suspense Account shall not be reckoned as part of provisions

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's PSL Directions, 2025, loans to individuals solely engaged in allied activities (with no land holding) count towards the Small and Marginal Farmers sub-target up to:

solution.explanation: SMFs include loans up to ₹2.5 lakh to individuals solely engaged in allied activities, without any accompanying land-holding criterion.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1.6 lakh, ₹5 lakh and ₹10 lakh are not the limit in this clause.

fact_checks.claim: Loans up to ₹2.5 lakh to individuals solely engaged in allied activities without any accompanying land holding criteria

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A domestic bank has met its overall PSL target but is short of its Micro Enterprises sub-target. Under RBI's PSLC guidelines in the PSL Directions, 2025, which certificate must it buy to cover this shortfall?

solution.concept: Matching PSLC type to the shortfall
solution.explanation: PSLC – Micro Enterprises counts towards the micro enterprises sub-target and the overall target. A bank short of a specific sub-target must buy the specific PSLC; PSLC – General counts only towards the overall target, and the agriculture and SF/MF certificates count towards farm targets.
steps: Buy the specific PSLC → PSLC – Micro Enterprises
solution.why_others_wrong: PSLC – General counts only for the overall target; agriculture and SF/MF certificates do not count for micro enterprises.

fact_checks.claim: PSLC - Micro Enterprises All PSL Loans to Micro Enterprises Achievement of micro-enterprise sub-target and overall PSL target; PSLC - General ... Achievement of overall PSL target
a bank having shortfall in achievement of any sub-target (e.g. SF/MF, Micro), will have to buy the specific PSLC to achieve the target

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank has purchased bills drawn under a letter of credit (payment to the beneficiary not under reserve). For computing 'bank credit in India' and ANBC for PSL, what do RBI's PSL FAQs say?

options.text: They are excluded from bank credit but may still be counted as PSL achievement
They count only if the LC-issuing bank is a scheduled commercial bank
They must not be excluded from bank credit in India; if the advance is PSL-eligible it can be classified as PSL
They are excluded as inter-bank exposure, since the LC-issuing bank bears the risk

solution.explanation: Such bills may be treated as inter-bank exposure only for computing exposure and capital requirements. They amount to bank credit to the borrower and must not be excluded from 'bank credit in India'; if the advance is eligible, the bank can classify it as PSL.
steps: Remains in bank credit in India / ANBC
solution.why_others_wrong: Exclusion from bank credit is not allowed; there is no condition about the type of LC-issuing bank.
solution.final_answer: Option C: They must not be excluded from bank credit in India; if the advance is PSL-eligible it can be classified as PSL

fact_checks.claim: The bills purchased/ discounted/ negotiated (payment to beneficiary not under reserve) under LC is allowed to be treated as interbank exposure only for the limited purpose of computing exposure and capital requirements. It should not be excluded from the computation of 'bank credit in India' ... If this advance is eligible for priority sector classification, the bank can classify it as PSL

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under a co-lending arrangement between a bank and an NBFC for priority sector loans, RBI's PSL FAQs explain what 'back-to-back basis' means. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The bank first opens the loan accounts, and the NBFC follows
Both open and fund their loan accounts simultaneously on a single date
The NBFC first opens the loan accounts, and the bank opens its share of the loan accounts subsequently
The NBFC retains 100% of the risk on the bank's share

solution.explanation: RBI clarified that back-to-back basis implies the loans are first opened by the NBFC and then the bank opens its loan accounts. It also said that PSL assets on the bank's books must at all times be without recourse to the NBFC.
steps: Bank's PSL assets: no recourse to NBFC
solution.why_others_wrong: The order is NBFC first; simultaneous opening is not what back-to-back means; the NBFC cannot carry the bank's risk, as the bank's PSL assets must be without recourse.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The NBFC first opens the loan accounts, and the bank opens its share of the loan accounts subsequently

fact_checks.claim: Back-to-back basis implies that the loans will be first opened by NBFC and then bank will open loan accounts subsequently
the priority sector assets on the bank's books should at all times be without recourse to the NBFC

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Bank D (domestic, ANBC ₹1,50,000 crore) has incremental export credit of ₹3,200 crore over the corresponding date of the previous year, of which ₹600 crore is to borrowers with sanctioned limits above ₹50 crore. Bank F (a foreign bank with 25 branches, ANBC ₹50,000 crore) has incremental export credit of ₹900 crore, of which ₹300 crore is to borrowers with sanctioned limits above ₹50 crore. ANBC is higher than CEOBSE for both, and none of this credit is to agriculture or MSMEs. How much export credit can each classify as priority sector?

solution.explanation: Domestic banks may count incremental export credit up to 2% of ANBC, with a sanctioned limit of up to ₹50 crore per borrower: (3,200 − 600) = 2,600, below 2% × 1,50,000 = 3,000, so ₹2,600 crore. Foreign banks with 20 or more branches may count incremental export credit up to 2% of ANBC without the per-borrower cap: 900, below 2% × 50,000 = 1,000, so ₹900 crore.
steps: D: exclude large-sanction borrowers → 2,600; cap 3,000 → ₹2,600 crore
F: no per-borrower cap → 900; cap 1,000 → ₹900 crore
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹3,000 crore for D ignores the ₹50 crore sanction limit; ₹600 crore for F wrongly applies that limit to a foreign bank with 20+ branches.
solution.final_answer: Option B: D: ₹2,600 crore; F: ₹900 crore

fact_checks.claim: Domestic banks/WoS of Foreign banks/SFBs/UCBs: Incremental export credit over corresponding date of the preceding year, up to 2 per cent of ANBC or CEOBSE whichever is higher, subject to a sanctioned limit of up to ₹50 crore per borrower. Foreign banks with 20 branches and above: Incremental export credit over corresponding date of the preceding year, up to 2 percent of ANBC or CEOBSE whichever is higher

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A domestic bank's ANBC (higher than CEOBSE) is ₹10,000 crore for all four quarters of a year, and its PSL target is 40%. Its own priority sector lending equals 37%, 38%, 38% and 39% of ANBC on the four quarterly reporting dates (30 June, 30 September, 31 December, 31 March). On 15 July it buys a PSLC – General of ₹100 crore. Following RBI's illustration on when a purchased PSLC is reckoned, and RBI's method for the annual shortfall, what is the bank's shortfall for the year?

solution.concept: Timing of PSLC reckoning and the annual shortfall
solution.explanation: A PSLC bought on 15 July is reckoned on the reporting dates of 30 September, 31 December and 31 March (not 30 June). ₹100 crore is 1% of ANBC, so achievements become 37, 39, 39 and 40%; quarterly shortfalls are 3, 1, 1 and 0. The year's shortfall is their simple average: 5 ÷ 4 = 1.25 percentage points.
steps: PSLC (1 pp) counts in Q2, Q3, Q4 only
solution.why_others_wrong: 2.00 ignores the PSLC; 1.00 counts it in the June quarter too; 0.25 takes only the last quarter's position.

fact_checks.claim: Bank A may sell PSLCs with a nominal value of ₹100 crores to Bank B on July 15, 2025. Bank B will reckon ₹100 crore towards its priority sector achievement as on the reporting dates of September 30, 2025, December 31, 2025 & March 31, 2026
The shortfall/ excess for the year is arrived at by taking a simple average of the shortfall/excess for all the four quarters

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: As a consumer protection measure under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, how should a Business Correspondent's retail outlet or sub-agent be introduced to the public?

options.text: Through an advertisement issued by the BC company
By an RBI notification listing all BC outlets
By the Gram Panchayat alone, without bank officials
Personally, by bank officials in a public meeting in the presence of village elders and government functionaries

solution.concept: Introducing BC outlets to the public
solution.explanation: To prevent misrepresentation or impersonation, the retail outlet/sub-agent must be personally introduced to the public by bank officials in the presence of village elders and government functionaries in a public meeting.
steps: Public meeting with village elders and officials
solution.why_others_wrong: An advertisement, an RBI list or a Panchayat-only introduction is not what the Directions require.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Personally, by bank officials in a public meeting in the presence of village elders and government functionaries

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following must a bank's arrangement with a Business Correspondent specify, under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025?

options.text: That the BC may charge customers a fee directly for services rendered for the bank
That financial services at the outlet may be tied to the sale of the BC company's products
Suitable limits on cash holding by the BC and on individual customer payments and receipts
That the BC may introduce its own products once it informs the bank

solution.explanation: Arrangements must specify limits on cash holding and on individual customer payments and receipts, issue of receipts on the bank's behalf, end-of-day accounting of off-line transactions and the bank's responsibility for the BC's acts. BCs cannot introduce products without the bank's approval, cannot tie services to their own products and cannot charge customers directly.
steps: Prohibited: own products, tie-ins, direct fees
solution.why_others_wrong: The other three are expressly prohibited.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Suitable limits on cash holding by the BC and on individual customer payments and receipts

fact_checks.claim: Suitable limits on cash holding by intermediaries as also limits on individual customer payments and receipts

the BC shall not introduce any product / process without the approval of the bank ... Financial services offered by the retail outlets / sub-agents of the BC shall not be tied to the sale of any product of such company

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to SBI's FAQs on PMJDY (describing RBI's BSBD guidelines), how many free withdrawals, including ATM transactions, must a BSBD account get every month at a minimum, and how are UPI, NEFT or IMPS payments treated?

options.text: Unlimited withdrawals at own-bank ATMs only
At least four; every UPI, NEFT or IMPS payment counts as one withdrawal
At least four; digital payments such as UPI, NEFT and IMPS are not counted as withdrawals
At least five; digital payments count as half a withdrawal

solution.explanation: A BSBD account gets a minimum of four free withdrawals and ATM transactions (own or other banks' ATMs) a month. Digital payments other than ATM transactions — PoS, NEFT, RTGS, UPI, IMPS and so on — are not counted as withdrawals for this purpose.
steps: Minimum four free withdrawals/ATM transactions a month
Digital payments excluded from the count
solution.why_others_wrong: Digital payments are not counted; five, half-counting and own-ATM-only are not the rule.
solution.final_answer: Option C: At least four; digital payments such as UPI, NEFT and IMPS are not counted as withdrawals

fact_checks.claim: Minimum of four free withdrawals and ATM transactions (done either at the bank's own ATM or another bank's ATM), in a month. Digital payment transactions excluding ATM transactions, i.e., Point of Sale transfers, NEFT, RTGS, UPI, IMPS, etc., shall not be counted as withdrawals for this purpose
