fact_checks.claim: In formulating the schemes on BC, the bank shall, inter alia, be guided by the recommendations made in Chapter III of the Khan Group Report

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How should transactions put through Business Correspondents normally be processed, under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025?

options.text: Through ICT devices integrated with the bank's CBS, accounted for in real time, with immediate verification to the customer
Through the BC company's own ledger, settled with the bank monthly
Only at the base Banking Outlet, with the BC collecting forms
In a paper register at the BC outlet, posted to CBS weekly

solution.explanation: Transactions should normally go through ICT devices (handheld devices or mobile phones) seamlessly integrated with the bank's Core Banking Solution, be accounted for in real time, and give customers immediate verification through the screen or a debit/credit slip.
solution.why_others_wrong: Weekly posting, BC ledgers and branch-only processing are contrary to the real-time CBS requirement.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Through ICT devices integrated with the bank's CBS, accounted for in real time, with immediate verification to the customer

fact_checks.claim: The transactions shall normally be put through ICT devices (handheld device/mobile phone) that are seamlessly integrated to the Core Banking Solution (CBS) of the bank. The transactions shall be accounted for on a real time basis and the customers shall receive immediate verification of their transactions through visuals (screen based) or other means (debit or credit slip)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Three PMJDY account holders with RuPay debit cards die in accidents. P opened her account in March 2017 and last used her card 40 days before the accident. Q opened his account in January 2020; his last transaction on any channel was 120 days before the accident. R opened his account in 2022 and made a balance enquiry at a CSP 10 days before the accident. Based on the Government's PM-JDY note and SBI's PMJDY FAQs, what accident insurance is payable?

options.text: P ₹2 lakh; Q ₹2 lakh; R ₹2 lakh
P ₹1 lakh; Q nil; R nil
P ₹1 lakh; Q nil; R ₹2 lakh
P ₹1 lakh; Q ₹2 lakh; R ₹2 lakh

solution.concept: Conditions for the RuPay card accident cover
solution.explanation: The cover is ₹1 lakh, enhanced to ₹2 lakh for new PMJDY accounts opened after August 2018. It is payable only if the cardholder made at least one successful financial or non-financial transaction on any channel within 90 days before the accident (including the accident date). P: old account, active → ₹1 lakh. Q: no transaction in 90 days → nil. R: new account; a balance enquiry is a non-financial transaction → ₹2 lakh.
steps: P: opened before Aug 2018, active → ₹1 lakh
R: opened after Aug 2018, non-financial transaction counts → ₹2 lakh
solution.why_others_wrong: Q fails the 90-day activity test; P's account predates the enhancement; R's balance enquiry counts.
solution.final_answer: Option C: P ₹1 lakh; Q nil; R ₹2 lakh

fact_checks.claim: Accident insurance cover of ₹1 lakh (enhanced to ₹2 lakhs to new PMJDY accounts opened after August2018) is available

Benefits of Insurance will be available to the Cardholders who have performed minimum one successful financial or non-financial transaction at any Channel ... within 90 days prior to date of accident including accident date for Rupay Cardholders

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about consumer protection in the Business Correspondent model under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025:
I. A BC may introduce a new product at its outlets without the bank's approval if it informs the base Banking Outlet.
II. The charges for various services must be indicated in a brochure available at the retail outlets or with the sub-agents.
III. The bank must have a business continuity plan to ensure uninterrupted service if the agency arrangement with the BC is terminated.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: Products and processes must be approved by the bank and the BC cannot introduce any product or process without that approval. Charges must be shown in a brochure at the outlets, and the bank must have a business continuity plan for uninterrupted service if the BC arrangement ends.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing I are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option B: II and III only

fact_checks.claim: The products and processes shall be approved by the bank and the BC shall not introduce any product / process without the approval of the bank

The charges for offering various services shall be indicated in a brochure and made available at the retail outlets / with the sub-agents ... The bank shall have necessary Business Continuity Plan (BCP) in place to ensure uninterrupted service in case the agency arrangement with the BCs / subagents is terminated

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025, banks may use Business Facilitators (BFs) and Business Correspondents (BCs). Consider the following statements:
I. Post offices appear in both the list of BF intermediaries and the list of entities eligible as BCs.
II. Krishi Vigyan Kendras are listed among the entities eligible to be engaged as BCs.
III. KVIC/KVIB units are listed among the intermediaries a bank may use under the BF model.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: The BF list includes NGOs/SHGs, farmers' clubs, co-operatives, community-based organisations, IT-enabled rural outlets of corporates, post offices, insurance agents, panchayats, village knowledge centres, agri-clinics, agri-business centres, Krishi Vigyan Kendras and KVIC/KVIB units. The BC list includes specified individuals, NGOs/MFIs, co-operative societies, post offices, payments banks, non-NBFC companies and NBFCs-ND — but not Krishi Vigyan Kendras.
steps: I: post offices are in both lists → correct
II: KVKs are in the BF list only → wrong
III: KVIC/KVIB units are BF intermediaries → correct
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing II are wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: Under the 'Business Facilitator' model, a bank may use the services of intermediaries such as: ... (vi) Post Offices ... (xii) Krishi Vigyan Kendras (xiii) KVIC/KVIB units

A bank may engage the following individuals / entities as BCs: (1) Individuals ... (2) NGOs / MFIs ... (3) Cooperative Societies ... (4) Post Offices (5) Payments Bank; and (6) Companies ... (7) Non-deposit taking NBFCs

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about remuneration and oversight of Business Correspondents under RBI's Branch Authorisation Directions, 2025:
I. The commission structure must be designed so that a mere increase in the number of clients or transaction volume does not drive the commission.
II. The Board (or its delegated committee) must review the operations of BCs at least once every six months, with a view to tapering down pre-funding by BCs.
III. Pre-funding should ideally come down, within two years of a BC starting operations, to around 30% of the limits for deposits and 15% for bank guarantees.
Which of the above are correct?

solution.explanation: Commission must not be driven merely by the number of clients or transactions; remuneration combines fixed and variable parts linked to customer satisfaction. The Board or its committee reviews BC operations at least every six months so that pre-funding tapers down, ideally to around 15% of the limits for deposits and 30% for bank guarantees within two years. Statement III swaps these figures.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options containing III are wrong because the percentages are reversed.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Commission structure or incentive mechanism shall be devised in a manner that mere increase in the number of clients served or the transaction volume does not drive the commission

The Board or any committee ... shall review the operations of BCs at least once every six months with a view to ensuring that requirement of prefunding ... should progressively taper down ... so as to reach around 15 percent of the limits fixed for each BC / CSP in case of deposits and 30 percent in case of Bank Guarantees, etc. in two years

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: During a period of financial stress, a bank uses part of its stock of HQLA and its LCR falls below 100 per cent. What does RBI's LCR framework require it to do?

options.text: Immediately report the shortfall to RBI's Department of Supervision, with reasons and corrective steps
Pay a penal rate of interest on the shortfall to RBI for every day of the shortfall
Stop all lending until the LCR is restored
Nothing, as the LCR is only a monitoring tool

solution.explanation: The LCR must normally be at least 100%, but in stress a bank may use its HQLA and let the ratio fall below 100%. It must then immediately report the shortfall to the Department of Supervision, RBI, with the reasons and the corrective steps initiated.
steps: LCR < 100% → immediate report to DoS with reasons and remedial steps
solution.why_others_wrong: The LCR is a binding minimum; RBI does not require a lending freeze or a daily penal charge for this.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Immediately report the shortfall to RBI's Department of Supervision, with reasons and corrective steps

fact_checks.claim: during a period of financial stress, a bank shall have the option to use its stock of HQLA and thereby allowing LCR to fall below 100 per cent. In such a case, the bank shall immediately report the shortfall to DoS, RBI. The report shall include reasons for such usage and corrective steps initiated

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: At what level does RBI's LCR framework apply to a foreign bank operating in India through branches?

options.text: It does not apply to foreign bank branches
On a standalone basis, for its Indian operations only
Only to its largest branch in India
On a consolidated basis for the global group

solution.explanation: The LCR applies to an Indian bank on a solo and a consolidated basis. For a foreign bank operating as branches in India it applies on a standalone basis, i.e. to its Indian operations only.
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI does not apply its LCR to the foreign bank's global group, to one branch only, or exempt the branches.
solution.final_answer: Option B: On a standalone basis, for its Indian operations only

fact_checks.claim: The LCR framework shall be applicable to an Indian bank on a standalone ('solo') as well as consolidated level. For a foreign bank operating as branch in India, the framework shall be applicable on standalone basis i.e., for Indian operations only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Basel Committee's post-crisis Basel III reforms were endorsed in December 2017 by its oversight body. What is that body?

options.text: The International Monetary and Financial Committee of the IMF
The Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS)

solution.explanation: The BIS notes that the post-crisis regulatory reforms were endorsed on 7 December 2017 by the Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS), the Basel Committee's oversight body.
solution.why_others_wrong: The G20, FATF and IMFC are not the Basel Committee's oversight body.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS)

fact_checks.claim: The post-crisis regulatory reforms were endorsed by the Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS), the Basel Committee's oversight body, on 7 December 2017

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's liquidity risk management directions draw on a Basel Committee document published after the global financial crisis. Which document, published in September 2008, is it?

options.text: International Convergence of Capital Measurement and Capital Standards
Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision
Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision

solution.explanation: RBI notes that, after the crisis, the BCBS published 'Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision' in September 2008, later reviewed in January 2019; its broad principles are reproduced in the Asset Liability Management Directions.
steps: September 2008 → Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision
solution.why_others_wrong: The Core Principles (1997), the 1988 Capital Accord and market-risk standards are different documents.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision

fact_checks.claim: the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) published 'Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision' in September 2008 and subsequently reviewed in January 2019

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements on Required Stable Funding (RSF) factors under RBI's NSFR rules:
I. Unencumbered SLR securities attract an RSF factor of 5%.
II. Physically traded commodities, including gold, attract an RSF factor of 85%.
III. Loans to financial institutions with a residual maturity of one year or more attract an RSF factor of 65%.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Unencumbered Level 1 assets and SLR securities get 5%; physical traded commodities including gold get 85%; loans to financial institutions with residual maturity of one year or more fall in the 100% category (the 65% factor is for other unencumbered loans of a year or more, excluding loans to financial institutions, such as loans to sovereigns and NDBs).
steps: III: FI loans ≥ 1 year → 100%, not 65% – wrong
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement III is false, so options including it are wrong; 'II only' misses the true statement I.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Assets assigned a 5 per cent RSF factor comprise (1) Unencumbered Level 1 assets ... (2) Unencumbered SLR securities; 85 per cent RSF factor: (7) Physical traded commodities, including gold

100 per cent RSF factor: All other assets not included in the above categories, including non-performing loans, loans to financial institutions with a residual maturity of one year or more, non-exchange traded equities, fixed assets

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Over the next 30 days a bank has these maturing secured loans: a reverse repo of ₹200 crore secured by Level 1 assets, a reverse repo of ₹100 crore secured by non-HQLA assets, and margin loans of ₹80 crore to customers against non-HQLA collateral. Under RBI's LCR rules, what total cash inflow can it recognise from these?

solution.concept: Inflows from secured lending in the LCR
solution.explanation: Maturing reverse repos secured by Level 1 assets are assumed to roll over, so 0% inflow. Those secured by non-HQLA are assumed not to roll over, so 100% (₹100 crore). For margin loans against non-HQLA collateral, no more than 50% of contractual inflows can be recognised (₹40 crore). Total = ₹140 crore.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹380 crore counts everything at 100%; ₹180 crore takes the margin loans at 100%; ₹100 crore ignores the margin loans.

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall assume that maturing reverse repurchase or securities borrowing agreements secured by Level 1 assets will be rolled over, and therefore will not give rise to any cash inflows, i.e., zero per cent cash inflow ... A bank is assumed not to roll-over maturing reverse repurchase or securities borrowing agreements secured by non-HQLA assets and can assume to receive back 100 per cent of the cash
a bank shall recognise no more than 50 per cent of contractual inflows from maturing margin loans made against non-HQLA collateral

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements on Basel III, based on the Bank for International Settlements' account:
I. The Basel Committee issued the full text of the revised Liquidity Coverage Ratio after its endorsement by the GHOS on 6 January 2013.
II. The first Basel III text was published in December 2012 and has not been updated since.
III. The Regulatory Consistency Assessment Programme (RCAP), which monitors implementation of Basel standards, was established in 2012.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The revised LCR text followed GHOS endorsement on 6 January 2013. The initial Basel III document was published in December 2010 and updated in June 2011, so statement II is wrong. The RCAP was set up in 2012 to monitor timely and consistent adoption of Basel III.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with II are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the correct statement III.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: The Basel Committee issued the full text of the revised Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) following endorsement on 6 January 2013 by its governing body - the Group of Central Bank Governors and Heads of Supervision (GHOS); This document, originally published in December 2010 and updated in June 2011 represents the initial phase of Basel III reforms
The Basel Committee established a comprehensive Regulatory Consistency Assessment Programme (RCAP) in 2012 to monitor and assess the adoption and implementation of its standards

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: After registering a complaint with the RBI Ombudsman, how can a complainant track its status on RBI's CMS portal?

options.text: Using the bank account number and IFSC
Only by visiting the Office of the RBI Ombudsman
Using the Aadhaar number and PAN
Using the complaint number and mobile number

solution.explanation: On successful registration the complainant gets a complaint number; the status can be tracked on the CMS portal with the complaint number and mobile number, or through the Contact Centre (14448).
steps: Complaint number + mobile number → status on CMS
solution.why_others_wrong: Account/IFSC and Aadhaar/PAN are not used; no office visit is needed.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Using the complaint number and mobile number

fact_checks.claim: The status of the complaint can be tracked through the CMS portal using the complaint number and mobile number

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25, about how many complaints were received under the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme in 2024-25?

solution.explanation: 13,34,244 complaints were received in 2024-25 against 11,75,075 in 2023-24, a rise of 13.55%. Of the total, 9.11 lakh came to the CRPC and 2.96 lakh to the Offices of RBI Ombudsman.
solution.why_others_wrong: 11.75 lakh is the 2023-24 figure; 9.11 lakh and 2.96 lakh are the CRPC and ORBIO parts.

fact_checks.claim: Under the RB-IOS, 13,34,244 complaints were received in F.Y.2024-25 as compared to 11,75,075 in F.Y.2023-24, an increase of 13.55 per cent over the previous year

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25, from which population group did the largest share of complaints received at the Offices of RBI Ombudsman come?

solution.explanation: In 2024-25, 45.86% of complaints came from metropolitan centres, followed by urban (25.64%), semi-urban (18.46%) and rural areas (10.04%).
solution.why_others_wrong: Urban, semi-urban and rural areas each had smaller shares.

fact_checks.claim: majority of complaints at the ORBIOs were received from Metropolitan Centres (45.86 per cent), followed by Urban (25.64 per cent), Semi Urban (18.46 per cent) and Rural areas (10.04 per cent)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25, which statement about complaints against banks received at the Offices of RBI Ombudsman is correct?

options.text: Public sector banks continued to have the highest share among banks, at over 38%
Complaints against NBFCs outnumbered those against banks
Private sector banks had the highest share among banks (37.53%), overtaking public sector banks (34.80%)
Small finance banks had the highest share among banks

solution.explanation: Banks accounted for 81.53% of complaints (NBFCs 14.80%). Among banks, the share of private sector banks rose from 34.39% to 37.53%, while that of public sector banks, the highest in 2023-24, fell from 38.32% to 34.80%.
solution.why_others_wrong: PSBs were highest only in 2023-24; SFBs were not the highest; NBFCs were far fewer than banks.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Private sector banks had the highest share among banks (37.53%), overtaking public sector banks (34.80%)

fact_checks.claim: Among the banks, the share of complaints received against private sector banks was the highest and increased from 34.39 per cent in F.Y.2023-24 to 37.53 per cent in F.Y.2024-25. However, the share of complaints received against the public sector banks, which was the highest in F.Y.2023-24, declined from 38.32 per cent in F.Y. 2023-24 to 34.80 per cent in F.Y.2024-25

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following banks is covered by RB-IOS, 2026?

options.text: A non-scheduled primary (urban) co-operative bank with deposits of ₹30 crore

solution.explanation: RB-IOS, 2026 covers all commercial banks, RRBs, State Co-operative Banks, Central Co-operative Banks, scheduled UCBs and non-scheduled UCBs with deposits of ₹50 crore and above. HFCs and CICs are among the excluded NBFC types.
solution.why_others_wrong: The UCB is below the ₹50 crore threshold; HFCs and CICs are expressly excluded.
solution.final_answer: Option D: A District Central Co-operative Bank

fact_checks.claim: Banks: all Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks, State Co-operative Banks, Central Co-operative Banks, Scheduled Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks, and Non-Scheduled Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks with deposit size of Rs 50 crore and above
NBFCs: all NBFCs registered with RBI, excluding Housing Finance Companies, Core Investment Companies

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25, the largest group of non-maintainable complaints closed by the Offices of RBI Ombudsman were 'First Resort Complaints'. What are these?

options.text: Complaints filed within the first 30 days of opening an account
Complaints filed with the RBI Ombudsman without the complainant first approaching the regulated entity
Complaints filed for the first time by a customer under any ombudsman scheme
Complaints first filed in a civil court

solution.explanation: FRCs are complaints received at the ORBIOs without the complainant having approached the concerned RE first. They are sent to the RE for redress, and the complainant is told he may complain again if the RE does not reply within 30 days or the reply is unsatisfactory. They formed 33.01% of the non-maintainable complaints closed by ORBIOs in 2024-25.
steps: No prior complaint to the RE → First Resort Complaint → sent to the RE
solution.why_others_wrong: The term has nothing to do with first-time complainants, new accounts or court cases.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Complaints filed with the RBI Ombudsman without the complainant first approaching the regulated entity

fact_checks.claim: Of these, 33.01 per cent (36,289 complaints) were closed as First Resort Complaints (FRCs) ... FRCs are those complaints which are received at the ORBIOs without the complainant having approached the concerned RE first

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Centralised Receipt and Processing Centre (CRPC) in 2024-25, as reported in RBI's Annual Report of the Ombudsman Scheme 2024-25:
I. Complaints received at the CRPC grew much faster (18.83%) than those received at the Offices of RBI Ombudsman (0.82%).
II. Most complaints disposed of at the CRPC were assigned to the Offices of RBI Ombudsman for examination.
III. E-mail was the channel for 93.18% of the complaints received at the CRPC.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: CRPC complaints rose 18.83% (7,66,957 to 9,11,384) while ORBIO complaints rose 0.82%. Of 9.04 lakh complaints disposed at the CRPC, only 1.20 lakh were assigned to ORBIOs/CEPCs; 7.84 lakh were closed at the CRPC as non-complaints or non-maintainable, mostly First Resort Complaints. 93.18% of CRPC complaints came by e-mail.
steps: II: wrong – 1.20 lakh of 9.04 lakh assigned
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II is false, which rules out the options containing it; 'III only' omits the correct statement I.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and III only

fact_checks.claim: The complaints received at the CRPC increased by 18.83 per cent from 7,66,957 complaints in F.Y.2023-24 to 9,11,384 complaints in F.Y.2024-25, while those received at the ORBIOs ... increased by 0.82 per cent

the CRPC has received 9.11 lakh complaints and disposed 9.04 lakh complaints ... Out of these, 1.20 lakh complaints were assigned to ORBIOs/CEPCs, while the remaining 7.84 lakh complaints were closed at the CRPC as non-complaint / non-maintainable complaints
During F.Y.2024-25, 93.18 per cent of the complaints received at the CRPC were through email

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026, what must a bank do about fake or malicious apps with names or features similar to its own mobile banking app?

options.text: Nothing, as app stores alone are responsible
Report them only in its annual report
Ask customers to verify apps by visiting a branch
Actively monitor popular app stores and the web for them and respond to get them taken down

solution.explanation: Banks must institute a mechanism to actively monitor popular app stores and the web for non-genuine, unauthorised or malicious applications with similar names or features, and respond appropriately to bring them down. They must also publish the checksum of their genuine app.
steps: Monitor app stores and the web → act to take down rogue apps
solution.why_others_wrong: The duty lies with the bank and calls for active monitoring and takedown, not passive reporting.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Actively monitor popular app stores and the web for them and respond to get them taken down

fact_checks.claim: The bank shall institute a mechanism to actively monitor for non-genuine / unauthorised / malicious applications (with similar name / features) on popular app-stores and the web and respond appropriately to bring them down

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: By what date did RBI require all payment system providers and participants to comply with its Authentication mechanisms for digital payment transactions Directions, 2025 (unless a provision specified otherwise)?

solution.explanation: The Directions, dated 25 September 2025 and issued under the PSS Act, 2007, required all payment system providers and participants, banks and non-banks, to comply by 1 April 2026. A separate deadline of 1 October 2026 applied to cross-border card-not-present validation.
solution.why_others_wrong: 25 September 2025 is the date of issue; 1 October 2026 is the cross-border CNP deadline; 1 January 2026 is not the date.

fact_checks.claim: All Payment System Providers and Payment System Participants, including banks and non-bank entities, shall ensure compliance with these directions by April 01, 2026, unless indicated otherwise for any specific provision herein

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An entity wishes to test a CBDC-related use case in RBI's CBDC and Asset Tokenisation (CAT) Sandbox. To which department of RBI should it send its request?

options.text: Department of Payment and Settlement Systems

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say interested entities submit a detailed request to the FinTech Department, RBI, by e-mail; after assessment and due diligence, the FinTech Department decides on granting access to the non-live sandbox environment.
steps: CAT Sandbox requests → FinTech Department, RBI
solution.why_others_wrong: The other departments do not handle CAT Sandbox access.

fact_checks.claim: Interested entities can submit their detailed request to the FinTech Department, RBI for accessing the CAT Sandbox by email at rbicbdcsandbox@rbi.org.in

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A customer pays an online merchant through a payment aggregator. Under RBI's Digital Payment Security Controls Directions, 2026, whose name should the bank's alert and OTP for this transaction show?

solution.explanation: Alerts and OTPs received by the customer for online transactions shall identify the merchant name, wherever applicable, rather than the payment aggregator through which the transaction was effected, so that the customer can recognise the payment.
steps: Alert/OTP → merchant name, not the aggregator
solution.why_others_wrong: Showing the aggregator, network or only the bank defeats the purpose of identifying the payee.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The merchant's name, wherever applicable

fact_checks.claim: The alerts and OTPs received by the customer for online transactions shall identify the merchant name, wherever applicable, rather than the payment aggregator through which the transaction was effected

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about customer conduct rules in RBI's Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025:
I. Banks must obtain the customer's explicit consent, duly recorded, for registering or de-registering for digital banking services.
II. Terms and conditions for registration should be in clear and simple language, preferably in English, Hindi and the local language.
III. Banks may obtain and record the mobile numbers of all customers to send transaction and other alerts.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: All three reproduce the Directions: explicit, recorded consent for registration (para 10.1); terms in clear, simple language, preferably English, Hindi and the local language (para 10.3); and, although no digital channel may be made compulsory for other facilities, banks can obtain and record mobile numbers of all customers to send alerts (para 10.5).
solution.why_others_wrong: Each of the other options leaves out at least one correct statement.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I, II and III

fact_checks.claim: Banks shall obtain explicit consent from the customer for registering/de-registering (in case of existing customers) for digital banking services and the consent shall be duly recorded/documented; For registration, banks shall provide the terms and conditions in clear and simple language (preferably in English, Hindi, and the local language)
The banks can, however, obtain and record mobile numbers of all customers to send transaction or other alerts

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A remitter wants to send money to Nepal through NEFT under the Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility. If the remitter holds an account with an NEFT-enabled bank branch in India, what additional identification documents must be submitted?

options.text: PAN card and a letter from the employer
Passport and visa of the remitter
Proof of the beneficiary's account with a Nepalese bank
None; no additional information, documents or identification is needed

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say a remitter who maintains an account with a bank branch in India need not give any additional information, documents or identification. A walk-in remitter must submit proof of identity such as passport, PAN, driving licence, telephone bill or employer's certificate.
solution.why_others_wrong: Identity documents are needed only from walk-in customers; the beneficiary need not hold a bank account.
solution.final_answer: Option D: None; no additional information, documents or identification is needed

fact_checks.claim: If the remitting customer maintains an account with a bank branch in India, there is no need for any additional information, documents or identification. Else, the remitter has to submit documents for proof of identification

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank in India and a bank in Nepal enter into their own bilateral arrangement to handle remittances between the two countries. According to RBI's FAQs, is this arrangement covered by the Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility Scheme?

options.text: Yes; all India–Nepal remittances by banks fall under INRF
Only if the Nepalese bank is a subsidiary of an Indian bank
No; INRF exclusively uses the NEFT ecosystem, and bilateral arrangements are outside its guidelines
Yes, if the Indian bank is a public sector bank

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say bilateral arrangements between banks or non-banks to handle India–Nepal cross-border transactions are not covered by the INRF guidelines; the scheme exclusively uses the NEFT ecosystem, and all NEFT-enabled branches are already covered.
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI states plainly that bilateral arrangements are not covered, irrespective of the banks' ownership.
solution.final_answer: Option C: No; INRF exclusively uses the NEFT ecosystem, and bilateral arrangements are outside its guidelines

fact_checks.claim: No. The bilateral arrangements between banks / non-banks to handle cross-border transactions between India and Nepal are not covered under guidelines of the INRF Scheme. The INRF Scheme exclusively uses NEFT ecosystem for such remittance to Nepal

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A walk-in customer paid cash at an Indian bank branch to send money to Nepal under INRF, but the money could not be delivered and has flowed back through NEFT. According to RBI's FAQs, how does the customer get the refund?

options.text: By applying to Nepal SBI Ltd, which refunds in Nepalese rupees
It is automatically credited to any bank account the customer names later
By producing evidence of the remittance, the counterfoil of the remittance application form
By filing a claim with RBI's NEFT Help Desk

solution.explanation: Undelivered amounts flow back through NEFT to the originating branch. If the remittance was made by debit to an account, the amount is credited back to that account; a walk-in remitter who paid cash must produce proof of remittance, the counterfoil of the application form, to get the refund.
steps: Account remitter → credited back to account
Walk-in cash remitter → refund against counterfoil
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no automatic credit to a new account, no refund in Nepal and no claim with RBI.
solution.final_answer: Option C: By producing evidence of the remittance, the counterfoil of the remittance application form

fact_checks.claim: If the remittance was made by a walk-in customer through a cash deposit, the remitter has to produce evidence of proof of remittance (counterfoil of the remittance application form) for getting refund

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Indo-Nepal Remittance Facility (INRF) Scheme, based on RBI's FAQs:
I. A sender who maintains an account with an NEFT-enabled branch faces no limit on the number of remittances in a year.
II. Of the ₹20 charged by SBI per remittance (up to ₹50,000), ₹10 is shared with Nepal SBI Ltd.
III. Nepal SBI Ltd charges an additional amount for crediting a beneficiary who holds an account with it.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Account-holding senders face no limit on the number of remittances (walk-in customers are limited to 12 a year) — I is correct. SBI's ₹20 is shared with NSBL at ₹10 each — II is correct. NSBL does not charge anything extra for crediting a beneficiary who has an account with it; the extra ₹50/₹75 applies only when the beneficiary has no NSBL account — III is wrong.
steps: III → wrong (extra only without NSBL account)
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'II only' wrongly rejects I.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: There is no limit on remittances if the sender is maintaining account with any NEFT enabled bank-branch in India

State Bank of India – ₹20/- per transaction. SBI would share this ₹20/- with NSBL at ₹10 each. NSBL would not charge any additional amount for crediting the beneficiary. if he maintains an account with it

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following is listed in RBI's RTGS FAQs as a benefit of using RTGS?

options.text: Transfers can be scheduled for any future date
There is no need to give the beneficiary's account number
RBI guarantees a minimum interest on the amount in transit

solution.explanation: RBI lists RTGS benefits such as safety, no amount cap set by RBI, 24x7x365 availability, real-time transfer, no need for physical cheques or drafts, capped charges and legal backing for the transaction.
steps: Benefits include: legal backing, capped charges, 24x7, real-time credit
solution.why_others_wrong: No interest is paid on transit funds; RTGS does not accept future value-dated transactions; the beneficiary account number is essential.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The transaction has legal backing

fact_checks.claim: The transaction charges have been capped by RBI. The transaction has legal backing

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), India's large value payment systems (LVPS) consist of RBI's RTGS and the systems operated by:

options.text: The Clearing Corporation of India Ltd (CCIL)
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)

solution.explanation: RBI describes LVPS (wholesale payment systems) as those for large-value, high-priority payments such as money market, securities and interbank settlements. In India they include RBI-operated RTGS and CCIL-operated systems: Government securities clearing, forex clearing and rupee derivatives.
steps: LVPS = RTGS (RBI) + CCIL systems (G-sec, forex, rupee derivatives)
solution.why_others_wrong: NPCI and NBBL run retail systems; IBA does not operate payment systems.
solution.final_answer: Option A: The Clearing Corporation of India Ltd (CCIL)

fact_checks.claim: In India, LVPS include RBI-operated system viz. Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) and systems operated by Clearing Corporation of India Limited (CCIL)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A businessman wants his bank to pull ₹10 lakh through RTGS from a customer's account in another bank, which owes him money. According to RBI's FAQs, can such a transaction be originated?

options.text: No; RTGS is a credit-push system and only the payer can originate a transfer to the beneficiary
Yes, but only on working days during business hours
Yes, if the amount is ₹2 lakh or more
Yes, if the debtor's bank gives positive confirmation

solution.explanation: RBI's FAQs say RTGS is a credit-push system: transactions can be originated only by the payer/remitter to pay funds to a beneficiary. A transaction cannot be originated to draw (receive) funds from another account.
solution.why_others_wrong: The amount, timing or positive confirmation does not change the credit-push design.
solution.final_answer: Option A: No; RTGS is a credit-push system and only the payer can originate a transfer to the beneficiary

fact_checks.claim: No. RTGS is a credit-push system i.e., transactions can be originated by the payer / remitter / sender only to pay / transfer / remit funds to a beneficiary

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's RTGS FAQs (updated October 2026):
I. No charge may be levied on inward RTGS transactions, and for outward ones banks may charge less than RBI's prescribed caps but not more.
II. With effect from 1 July 2019, RBI waived the processing charges it levied on banks for RTGS, and banks may pass the benefit on to customers.
III. To initiate an RTGS transfer, the remitter must hand over a physical cheque or demand draft at the branch.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Inward RTGS transactions are free, and banks may charge less than RBI's caps on outward ones but not more (I correct). RBI waived its own processing charges from 1 July 2019 so that banks could pass on the benefit (II correct). RBI lists as a benefit that the remitter need not use a physical cheque or draft, and can initiate RTGS through internet or mobile banking (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: a) Inward transactions – Free, no charge to be levied ... Banks may decide to charge a lower rate but cannot charge more than the rates prescribed by RBI
With effect from July 01, 2019, RBI has waived the processing charges levied by it for RTGS transactions. Banks may pass on the benefit to its customers
The remitter need not use a physical cheque or a demand draft

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: As described in RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), IMPS, introduced by NPCI, supports which kinds of transactions?

options.text: Both person-to-person and person-to-merchant transactions, with real-time credit, 24x7
Only person-to-person transfers, settled in half-hourly batches
Only bulk salary and pension credits
Only large-value interbank transfers of ₹2 lakh and above

solution.explanation: The report describes IMPS as a fast payment system introduced by NPCI, offering 24x7 instant fund transfers through mobile banking, internet banking and ATMs, giving real-time credit to beneficiaries' accounts and supporting both person-to-person and person-to-merchant transactions.
solution.why_others_wrong: Half-hourly batches describe NEFT; bulk credits describe NACH; ₹2 lakh minimum describes RTGS.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both person-to-person and person-to-merchant transactions, with real-time credit, 24x7

fact_checks.claim: Immediate Payment Service (IMPS): IMPS is a fast payment system introduced by NPCI, offering 24x7 instant fund transfer through multiple channels including mobile banking, internet banking, and ATMs. It enables real-time credit to beneficiaries' accounts and supports both person-to-person and person-to-merchant transactions

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: How does RBI describe the turn-around times (TAT) it prescribed in 2019 for resolving failed transactions in systems such as IMPS?

options.text: As the minimum period a bank must wait before reversing a failed transaction
As applicable only to complaints routed through the RBI Ombudsman
As the outer limit for resolution, with banks and operators expected to resolve failures sooner
As indicative targets that banks may extend with Board approval

solution.explanation: RBI's circular of 20 September 2019 notes that the prescribed TAT is the outer limit for resolution of failed transactions and that banks and other operators/participants shall endeavour towards quicker resolution. It came into effect from 15 October 2019.
solution.why_others_wrong: It is a maximum, not a waiting period; banks cannot extend it; it applies to all failed transactions, not only Ombudsman cases.
solution.final_answer: Option C: As the outer limit for resolution, with banks and operators expected to resolve failures sooner

fact_checks.claim: the prescribed TAT is the outer limit for resolution of failed transactions; and the banks and other operators / system participants shall endeavour towards quicker resolution of such failed transactions

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), IMPS volume rose from 434 crore transactions in CY 2021 to 518 crore in CY 2025, and value from ₹38 lakh crore to ₹75 lakh crore. Using these figures over the four years, which compound annual growth rates (CAGR) are closest?

options.text: Volume about 4.8% a year; value about 24.3% a year
Volume about 19% a year; value about 4.5% a year
Volume about 1.1% a year; value about 4.6% a year
Volume about 4.5% a year; value about 18.5% a year

solution.explanation: CAGR = (end ÷ start)^(1/years) − 1 over 4 years. Volume: (518 ÷ 434)^0.25 − 1 ≈ 4.5%. Value: (75 ÷ 38)^0.25 − 1 ≈ 18.5%; RBI, using unrounded data, reports 4.5% and 18.1%. Slow volume growth with fast value growth means IMPS is used for larger transfers.
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option swaps the two; 4.8% and 24.3% are simple averages (total growth ÷ 4); 1.1% and 4.6% divide the CAGR by four again.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Volume about 4.5% a year; value about 18.5% a year

fact_checks.claim: IMPS transactions volume rose from 434 crore in CY 2021 to 518 crore in CY 2025. More notably, transaction value doubled during the same period from ₹38 lakh crore to ₹75 lakh crore ( Chart 10 ). This translates into a CAGR of 4.5 per cent in in volume and 18.1 per cent in value

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's framework for small value digital payments in offline mode, which governs UPI Lite, on what basis are payment instruments enabled for offline transactions?

options.text: The explicit consent of the customer
On NPCI's instructions to all banks
Automatically for every customer of the bank

solution.explanation: The framework says payment instruments shall be enabled for offline transactions based on the explicit consent of the customer; offline payments are made in proximity mode and may be offered without AFA.
steps: Offline capability → only with the customer's explicit consent
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI requires the customer's explicit consent, not automatic, merchant-driven or NPCI-driven enabling.
solution.final_answer: Option B: The explicit consent of the customer

fact_checks.claim: Payment instruments shall be enabled for offline transactions based on explicit consent of the customer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In October 2024, RBI raised the per-transaction limit of UPI123Pay, the UPI facility for feature-phone users, to:

solution.explanation: In the October 2024 policy, RBI decided to enhance the per-transaction limit in UPI123Pay from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, along with raising UPI Lite limits.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹5,000 was the earlier limit; ₹1,000 is the UPI Lite per-transaction limit; ₹1 lakh is the general UPI limit.

fact_checks.claim: it has been decided to (i) enhance the per-transaction limit in UPI123Pay from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: UPI Lite is covered by RBI's framework for small value digital payments in offline mode. In what sense is a UPI Lite transaction 'offline', according to RBI?

options.text: It works without any connectivity at both the payer's and the payee's end
To the extent that AFA is not required and transaction alerts are not sent in real time
It is settled in cash at the end of the day
It is not recorded by the issuing bank at all

solution.explanation: RBI's framework notes that a UPI Lite transaction is offline to the extent that the Additional Factor of Authentication is not required and transaction alerts are not sent in real time. Issuers must still convey details of each transaction adequately.
solution.why_others_wrong: RBI does not describe UPI Lite as connectivity-free, cash-settled or unrecorded.
solution.final_answer: Option B: To the extent that AFA is not required and transaction alerts are not sent in real time

fact_checks.claim: UPI Lite transaction is offline to the extent that AFA is not required, and transaction alerts not sent in real time

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A customer has set a daily UPI limit of ₹10,000 in her banking app, and her UPI AutoPay mandate debits ₹12,000. Under RBI's Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, are payments under the e-mandate subject to her own limit?

options.text: Yes; the debit fails and the mandate is cancelled
No; payments under e-mandates are not subject to any other limits or controls set by the customer
Only if the mandate was registered after 2024
Yes; the debit must be split to stay within her limit

solution.explanation: The framework says payments under e-mandates shall not be subject to any other limits or controls set by the customer. The customer is protected instead by AFA at registration, pre-transaction notification with an opt-out, and the overall AFA-free caps.
solution.why_others_wrong: The framework explicitly excludes customer-set limits; no splitting or cancellation follows.
solution.final_answer: Option B: No; payments under e-mandates are not subject to any other limits or controls set by the customer

fact_checks.claim: Payments under e-mandates shall not be subject to any other limits / controls set by the customer

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about RBI's Framework for Facilitating Small Value Digital Payments in Offline Mode (updated December 2024), under which UPI Lite operates:
I. Apart from UPI Lite, an offline payment is capped at ₹500 per transaction and ₹2,000 in total on a payment instrument at any time.
II. Offline payments may be made only in proximity (face-to-face) mode.
III. Offline payments are outside RBI's circulars on limited customer liability.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The general offline limits are ₹500 per transaction and ₹2,000 in total (UPI Lite has higher limits) — I correct. Offline payments are allowed in proximity (face-to-face) mode only — II correct. They are covered by RBI's limited customer liability circulars, and customers can use the Integrated Ombudsman Scheme — III wrong.
steps: III → wrong (covered by limited liability rules)
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'II only' misses I.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: The upper limit of an offline payment transaction shall be ₹500. The total limit for offline transactions on a payment instrument shall be ₹2,000 at any point in time
Offline payments shall be made in proximity (face to face) mode only
Offline payments shall be covered under the provisions of RBI's limited customer liability circulars

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the INR prepaid wallets linked to UPI that RBI allows for foreign nationals and NRIs visiting India:
I. To start with, the facility is for travellers from G-20 countries arriving at select international airports.
II. The PPI is issued after physical verification of the customer's passport and visa at the point of issue.
III. The wallet can be loaded only against Indian rupee cash.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI's PPI Master Direction allows full-KYC INR PPIs to foreign nationals/NRIs visiting India, starting with G-20 travellers at select international airports (I correct), after physical verification of passport and visa (II correct). Loading is against receipt of foreign exchange by cash or any payment instrument, with rupee conversion only by authorised dealers (III wrong). Unused balances can be encashed in foreign currency or sent back to source.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option C: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: to start with, this facility will be extended to travellers from the G-20 countries, arriving at select international airports ... The PPIs shall be issued after physical verification of Passport and Visa of the customers at the point of issuance
Loading / Reloading of such PPIs shall be against receipt of foreign exchange by cash or through any payment instrument

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about NPCI's UPI changes that took effect from 1 August 2025:
I. Within a 30-day window, a user can raise only 10 payment reversal requests, and only five against the same sender.
II. The name linked to the recipient's account is displayed before the payer enters the UPI PIN.
III. A user can request the list of bank accounts linked to her mobile number up to 50 times a day on each app.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: From 1 August 2025, only 10 payment reversal requests are allowed in 30 days, with a cap of five per sender (I correct); the official name of the recipient's account is shown before the PIN is entered (II correct). Requests for the list of linked bank accounts are capped at 25 a day; 50 is the balance-enquiry cap (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III confuse the account-list cap with the balance-enquiry cap; 'II only' misses I.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: within a 30-day window, only 10 payment reversal requests are allowed. However, there is also a cap on requests with each sender at five in the same time period
the official name linked to the recipient's account will be displayed before you hit your UPI PIN
users can only have 25 daily requests for getting the bank details associated with their phone number

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Digital Payments – E-mandate Framework, 2026, which governs UPI AutoPay:
I. Every e-mandate must specify its validity period, and the customer can modify the period or withdraw the mandate at any time.
II. For a variable-amount e-mandate, the customer can specify the maximum value of any recurring transaction.
III. The issuer may levy a nominal charge on the customer for the e-mandate facility.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Each e-mandate must specify its validity period, and the issuer must allow the customer to modify it or withdraw the mandate at any time (I correct). For variable e-mandates the customer can set the maximum value of any recurring transaction (II correct). No charges may be levied for availing the e-mandate facility (III wrong).
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' misses II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Every e-mandate registered by the issuer shall specify the validity period of the e-mandate. The issuer shall provide the customer with a facility to modify the validity period or withdraw the e-mandate at any point of time
In the case of variable e-mandates, the issuer shall provide the customer with a facility to specify the maximum value of any recurring transaction
No charges shall be levied to the customer for availing the e-mandate facility for recurring transactions

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's directions of June 2025 on the Aadhaar Enabled Payment System, an 'AePS Touchpoint Operator (ATO)' is:

options.text: The NPCI unit that settles AePS transactions
The UIDAI official who verifies biometrics
The individual onboarded by the acquiring bank who operates the AePS touchpoint
The company that manufactures micro-ATM terminals

solution.explanation: The directions define the AePS touchpoint as the terminal (mobile or fixed) deployed by acquirer banks for AePS transactions, and the ATO as the individual onboarded by the acquiring bank who operates it.
steps: Touchpoint = terminal deployed by acquirer bank
ATO = individual operating it, onboarded by that bank
solution.why_others_wrong: Device makers, UIDAI and NPCI are not ATOs.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The individual onboarded by the acquiring bank who operates the AePS touchpoint

fact_checks.claim: AePS Touchpoint Operator (ATO): The individual onboarded by the acquiring bank who operates the AePS touchpoint

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's AePS directions, which aspects must form part of an acquiring bank's fraud risk management framework when it monitors AePS touchpoint operators?

options.text: Location and type of the ATO and the volume and velocity of transactions
Only the ATO's income tax returns
Only the number of customers the ATO personally knows

solution.explanation: The acquiring bank must monitor ATOs through its transaction monitoring systems on an ongoing basis and set operational parameters based on their business risk profile; aspects such as location and type of the ATO and the volume and velocity of transactions form part of its fraud risk management framework, and the parameters are reviewed periodically for emerging fraud trends.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options are not what RBI prescribes.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Location and type of the ATO and the volume and velocity of transactions

fact_checks.claim: Aspects such as location and type of the ATO, volume and velocity of transactions, etc. shall form part of bank's fraud risk management framework

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), what recent enhancement has been made to the Bharat Bill Payment System, operated by NPCI's subsidiary NBBL?

options.text: Removal of insurance premiums from BBPS
Settlement of bill payments in foreign currency within India
Payment of bills only through bank branches
A cross-border bill payment facility that lets NRIs pay utility, education and other bills in India for their families

solution.explanation: RBI notes that a recent BBPS enhancement is a cross-border bill payment facility allowing Non-Resident Indians to pay utility, education and other bills in India on behalf of their families.
steps: BBPS → cross-border inward bill payments by NRIs
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no foreign-currency settlement within India, branch-only restriction or removal of insurance.
solution.final_answer: Option D: A cross-border bill payment facility that lets NRIs pay utility, education and other bills in India for their families

fact_checks.claim: A recent enhancement to BBPS includes a cross-border bill payment facility that allows Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) to pay utility, education, and other bills in India on behalf of their families

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Match each failed transaction with the turn-around time (TAT) rule in RBI's harmonised framework:
1. Account debited but cash not dispensed at an ATM or micro-ATM
2. AePS: account debited but confirmation not received at the merchant location
3. NACH: account debited despite the customer having revoked the debit mandate with the bank
4. PPI on-us: PPI debited but the beneficiary's PPI not credited
P. Pro-active reversal within T + 5 days
Q. Acquirer to initiate 'Credit Adjustment' within T + 5 days
R. Customer's bank responsible; resolution within T + 1 day
S. Reversal in the remitter's account within T + 1 day

solution.explanation: ATM/micro-ATM cash not dispensed → pro-active reversal within T + 5. AePS merchant confirmation not received → acquirer's 'Credit Adjustment' within T + 5. NACH debit despite mandate revocation → the customer's bank is responsible and must resolve within T + 1. PPI on-us failure → reversal in the remitter's account within T + 1. Each carries ₹100 per day for delay beyond the TAT where compensation applies.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options swap the ATM and AePS rules or the NACH and PPI rules.

fact_checks.claim: Customer's account debited but cash not dispensed. Pro-active reversal (R) of failed transaction within a maximum of T + 5 days
Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (including Aadhaar Pay) a Account debited but transaction confirmation not received at merchant location. Acquirer to initiate 'Credit Adjustment' within T + 5 days
Account debited despite revocation of debit mandate with the bank by the customer. Customer's bank will be responsible for such debit. Resolution to be completed within T + 1 day
On-Us transaction Beneficiary's PPI not credited. PPI debited but transaction confirmation not received at merchant location. Reversal effected in Remitter's account within T + 1 day

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's Payment Systems Report (December 2025), how did AePS fund transfers and BHIM Aadhaar Pay transactions grow between CY 2021 and CY 2025?

options.text: Rapidly: volume grew more than ten times, like UPI
They declined in both volume and value, like debit card transactions
Slowly: volume from 212 lakh to 231 lakh and value from ₹5,697 crore to ₹7,422 crore (CAGR about 2% and 7%)
Volume grew about 7% a year while value fell

solution.explanation: RBI reports that AePS (fund transfers) and BHIM Aadhaar Pay volume rose from 212 lakh in CY 2021 to 231 lakh in CY 2025 and value from ₹5,697 crore to ₹7,422 crore, CAGRs of 2.1% in volume and 6.8% in value.
solution.why_others_wrong: Growth was modest, not tenfold; neither measure declined.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Slowly: volume from 212 lakh to 231 lakh and value from ₹5,697 crore to ₹7,422 crore (CAGR about 2% and 7%)

fact_checks.claim: The volume of transactions conducted through AePS (fund transfers) and BHIM Aadhaar Pay increased from 212 lakh in CY 2021 to 231 lakh in CY 2025. The corresponding value of these transactions rose from ₹5,697 crore to ₹7,422 crore over the same period ... a CAGR of 2.1 per cent in volume and 6.8 per cent in value

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: From when did RBI's Payments Banks – Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025 come into effect?

solution.concept: Digital banking directions for payments banks
solution.explanation: The Directions, issued on 28 November 2025 as part of RBI's consolidation, came into effect on 1 January 2026. They govern internet and mobile banking (view-only and transactional) by payments banks.
solution.why_others_wrong: 28 November 2025 is the issue date; the other dates are not the effective date.

fact_checks.claim: These Directions shall come into effect from January 01, 2026. The provisions of these Directions shall be applicable to Payments Banks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: For applying the ₹10 crore exposure threshold in RBI's current account rules (as in the Payments Banks – Miscellaneous Directions), which lenders make up the 'banking system'?

options.text: All banks including payments banks, and all NBFCs
Commercial banks (including SFBs, LABs and RRBs, but excluding payments banks), urban co-operative banks and rural co-operative banks

solution.explanation: 'Banking System' covers commercial banks (including SFBs, LABs and RRBs but excluding payments banks), urban co-operative banks and rural co-operative banks (state and central co-operative banks). Payments banks are excluded because they do not lend.
steps: Include: commercial banks (SFB, LAB, RRB), UCBs, StCBs/CCBs
solution.why_others_wrong: NBFCs and AIFIs are outside the definition; payments banks are expressly excluded; co-operative banks are included.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Commercial banks (including SFBs, LABs and RRBs, but excluding payments banks), urban co-operative banks and rural co-operative banks

fact_checks.claim: 'Banking System' for the purpose of this Chapter shall include Commercial Banks (including Small Finance Banks, Local Area Banks, and Regional Rural Banks, but excluding Payments Banks), Urban Co-operative Banks and Rural Co-operative Banks (State Co-operative Banks and Central Co-operative Banks)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which of the following accounts is exempt from the 'collection account only' restriction for customers with banking system exposure of ₹10 crore or more?

options.text: An account with a balance below ₹2 lakh
An account opened as required under FEMA
Any account of a listed company

solution.explanation: Exempt accounts include accounts under FEMA, accounts or transactions stipulated by a statute or by a financial sector regulator or government, and accounts of regulated entities used for their regulated activities. Listing, a small balance or account age do not exempt an account.
steps: Exempt: FEMA accounts; statute/regulator-mandated; REs' regulated-activity accounts
solution.why_others_wrong: The other conditions are not exemptions.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Under IRDAI's July 2026 amendments, which of these holding companies may amalgamate into the insurer it holds?
P. Holds 60% of the insurer; has no other business; consideration in equity shares.
Q. Holds 60% of the insurer; also runs a software business.
R. Holds 45% of the insurer; has no other business.
S. Holds 70% of the insurer; has no other business; consideration partly in cash.

solution.concept: Amalgamation of a non-insurance entity into an insurer
solution.explanation: A non-insurance transferor may amalgamate with the insurer if it holds more than 50% of the insurer's paid-up equity and has no other non-insurance business, and only equity may be paid as consideration. Q has another business, R holds only 45%, and S proposes cash; only P qualifies.
steps: > 50% ✓, no other business ✓, equity only ✓ → P
solution.why_others_wrong: Q, R and S each fail one condition.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An insurer makes a rights issue. Shareholder X, holding 8%, does not subscribe and is diluted to 6.5%. How do IRDAI's July 2026 amendments treat this?

options.text: It is ignored, since X sold nothing
X must buy back shares to restore 8%
It needs SEBI's approval, not IRDAI's
The fall in X's holding from non-subscription is treated as shares intended to be transferred, so the transferor thresholds must be checked

solution.explanation: A decrease in a shareholder's holding due to non-subscription on a pro-rata basis in a fresh equity issue is treated as shares intended to be transferred. Here 1.5% of capital is deemed transferred; it is within the 5% per-year transferor threshold, but the rule means every existing holder's position must be modelled.
solution.why_others_wrong: The dilution is not ignored; SEBI does not approve; no buy-back obligation exists.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The fall in X's holding from non-subscription is treated as shares intended to be transferred, so the transferor thresholds must be checked

fact_checks.claim: a decrease in a shareholder's shareholding pursuant to non-subscription on a pro-rata basis in a fresh issuance of equity shares is also treated as shares intended to be transferred

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about PMSBY, based on the Department of Financial Services' FAQs:
I. Death of the insured by murder is covered.
II. A partial disability without irrecoverable loss of sight of an eye or use of a hand or foot gets ₹50,000.
III. A PMSBY cover is in addition to any other insurance cover the subscriber has.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: I is correct: death by murder is covered (suicide is not). II is wrong: no benefit is payable for partial disability without such irrecoverable loss. III is correct: PMSBY cover is in addition to other insurance.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with II is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and III only

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under SEBI's mutual fund categorisation (February 2026), what minimum share of its total assets must an index fund or ETF invest in the securities of the index it tracks?

solution.explanation: Index funds and ETFs, grouped under 'Other Schemes', must invest at least 95% of total assets in the securities of the index being replicated or tracked. Fund of funds must likewise put at least 95% in the underlying fund.
steps: Index fund / ETF ≥ 95% in index securities

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: SEBI's February 2026 categorisation introduced sectoral debt funds, which must invest at least 80% in AA+ and above rated debt of a particular sector. In which of the following sectors is such a fund NOT permitted?

solution.explanation: Sectoral debt funds may be launched only in Financial Services, Energy, Infrastructure, Housing and Real Estate, and only where enough investment-grade paper of that sector is available. Telecommunications is not on the list.
steps: Permitted: Financial Services, Energy, Infrastructure, Housing, Real Estate
solution.why_others_wrong: Housing, Energy and Real Estate are all on the permitted list.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: An Overnight Fund invests in securities maturing in one day. Under SEBI's February 2026 categorisation, what exception is allowed?

options.text: Up to 5% of net assets may be invested in listed equity for liquidity
Up to 5% of net assets may be placed in G-secs or T-bills with residual maturity of up to 30 days, for use as margin and collateral
Up to 20% of net assets may be held in liquid fund units
Up to 10% of net assets may be placed in commercial paper of up to 91 days for higher yield

solution.explanation: Overnight funds may deploy not more than 5% of net assets in G-secs and/or T-bills with residual maturity of up to 30 days, only to place them as margin and collateral for certain transactions.
steps: Overnight securities (1 day) + up to 5% in G-sec/T-bill ≤ 30 days for margin
solution.why_others_wrong: CP, liquid fund units and equity are not permitted under this exception.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Up to 5% of net assets may be placed in G-secs or T-bills with residual maturity of up to 30 days, for use as margin and collateral

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

solution.explanation: With 3–5 years to maturity, a Life Cycle Fund must hold 35–50% in equity, 25–50% in debt and 0–10% in gold/silver ETFs, ETCDs and InvITs. Only 45/45/10 meets all three ranges.

solution.final_answer: Option D: Equity 45%, debt 45%, gold/silver ETFs 10%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

Immunity from tax where the value is less than ₹50 lakh, from 1 April 2026
Immunity from prosecution where the aggregate value is less than ₹20 lakh, with retrospective effect from 1 October 2024
Immunity from prosecution for all such assets, whatever their value

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness

Profit margin of 15% on cost, giving tax of about 5%
Profit margin of 15.5%, giving tax of about 4%
Profit margin of 5% of invoice value, giving tax of about 2%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Economic Survey 2025-26 put the Centre's effective capital expenditure for FY26 at ₹15.48 lakh crore, and the Budget estimates it at ₹17.15 lakh crore (4.4% of GDP) for FY27, made up of capital expenditure of ₹12.22 lakh crore and grants for creation of capital assets of ₹4.93 lakh crore. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Effective capex is budgeted to grow by about 10.8%, and grants for capital assets make up about 29% of it
Effective capex equals capital expenditure minus grants for capital assets
Effective capex is budgeted to grow by about 1.67%, and grants make up about 40% of it
Effective capex is budgeted to fall, because grants are revenue expenditure

solution.explanation: Effective capex = capital expenditure + grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets = 12.22 + 4.93 = ₹17.15 lakh crore. Growth over FY26: (17.15 − 15.48) ÷ 15.48 ≈ 10.8%. Share of grants: 4.93 ÷ 17.15 ≈ 28.7%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.67 is the increase in lakh crore, not per cent; effective capex rises; grants are added, not subtracted.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Effective capex is budgeted to grow by about 10.8%, and grants for capital assets make up about 29% of it

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Reassessment has been started against a taxpayer for a year in which his income was taxable at 30%. He now wants to update his return to show ₹10 lakh of omitted income. Under the Union Budget 2026-27 proposal (ignoring cess, surcharge and interest), what tax does he pay on it?

options.text: ₹6 lakh, i.e. 30% plus 100% of that tax as additional tax
₹3.3 lakh, i.e. 30% plus 10% of the tax
₹4 lakh, i.e. 30% plus an additional 10 percentage points

solution.explanation: Returns can be updated even after reassessment starts, at an additional 10 percent tax rate over and above the applicable rate: 30% + 10% = 40% of ₹10 lakh = ₹4 lakh.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹3 lakh omits the additional rate; ₹6 lakh applies the misreporting-immunity condition (100% additional tax); ₹3.3 lakh reads the 10% as a surcharge on tax instead of extra rate points.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹4 lakh, i.e. 30% plus an additional 10 percentage points

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements on the penalty and prosecution proposals of the Union Budget 2026-27:
I. Immunity from penalty and prosecution, available for under-reporting, is extended to misreporting of income, on payment of 100% of the tax amount as additional income tax over the tax and interest due.
II. Assessment and penalty proceedings are to be integrated through a common order.
III. Non-production of books of account is made a cognizable offence.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: I is correct: misreporting cases can get immunity by paying 100% of the tax as additional income tax (so a ₹6 lakh tax on misreported income means ₹12 lakh plus interest). II is correct. III is wrong: non-production of books of account and documents is to be decriminalised.
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option with III is wrong.
solution.final_answer: Option A: I and II only

Yes, but only for road accidents

solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1 lakh and ₹2 lakh are disability/death benefits, not hospitalisation cover; there is no road-accident-only reimbursement.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What does the 'Hybrid / Partial Collateral Security' product of CGTMSE allow?

options.text: CGTMSE and NCGTC may jointly guarantee the same loan
The borrower may pledge mutual fund units instead of paying the guarantee fee
The lender may take third-party guarantees for the whole loan and still get CGTMSE cover
The lender may take collateral for part of the loan and cover the unsecured part under CGS-I, up to ₹10 crore

solution.explanation: Under the hybrid model, MLIs may obtain collateral for part of the credit and get the remaining unsecured part (up to a maximum of ₹10 crore) covered by CGTMSE, which has a notional second charge on the collateral. Credit already covered through NCGTC is not eligible.
solution.why_others_wrong: Third-party guarantees make a loan ineligible; there is no fee-for-pledge option; NCGTC-covered credit is excluded.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The lender may take collateral for part of the loan and cover the unsecured part under CGS-I, up to ₹10 crore

fact_checks.claim: 'Hybrid Security' product has been introduced where the MLIs will be allowed to obtain collateral security for a part of the credit facility, whereas the remaining unsecured part of the credit facility, upto a maximum of ₹ 10 crore, can be covered under CGS-I. CGTMSE will, however, have notional second charge on the collateral security

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: For how long does a CGTMSE guarantee cover a borrower who has been given only working capital facilities?

options.text: For 18 months, the lock-in period, and then it ends
For a block of 5 years, which can be renewed, with no overall cap on the coverage period
For 10 years, and it cannot be renewed
Only for one year at a time, like the annual fee

solution.concept: Tenure of guarantee for working capital
solution.explanation: For term credit the cover runs through the agreed tenure; where working capital alone is given, cover is for 5 years or a block of 5 years. It can be renewed after the initial block, and there is no maximum coverage period for working capital accounts.
steps: WC only → 5-year blocks, renewable, no overall cap
solution.why_others_wrong: 18 months is the lock-in for claims; 10 years and one year are not the scheme's periods.
solution.final_answer: Option B: For a block of 5 years, which can be renewed, with no overall cap on the coverage period

fact_checks.claim: Where working capital alone is extended to the eligible borrower, the guarantee cover shall be for a period of 5 years or a block of 5 years ... Guarantee for working capital account can be renewed after completion of initial 5 years block coverage. There is no maximum guarantee coverage period cap for working capital account

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What happens under CGTMSE's CGS-I if a lending institution does not pay the annual guarantee fee demanded for a covered loan by the due date (normally 30 March)?

options.text: The borrower's account is automatically classified as NPA
The fee is simply recovered from the claim amount later
The cover continues, but the fee doubles
The Trust's liability for that credit facility lapses; revival may be sought within the next financial year with penal interest

solution.explanation: If the annual fee is not paid in time, the Trust's liability for that credit facility lapses. A request for revival must be made within the next financial year, the account must be standard, and dues are charged with penal interest at 4% over Bank Rate and an additional risk premium.
steps: Revival: next FY, standard account, penal interest
solution.why_others_wrong: The fee is not netted from claims, does not just double, and has no effect on the borrower's asset classification.
solution.final_answer: Option D: The Trust's liability for that credit facility lapses; revival may be sought within the next financial year with penal interest

A loan already covered for guarantee through NCGTC Ltd
A collateral-free term loan to a micro enterprise in retail trade
A working capital limit given without collateral to a small manufacturing unit
